sections.h2: Does Michigan still have an inheritance tax?
sections.html:
Only for old estates. Michigan Treasury says the inheritance tax remains in effect solely for people who inherited from someone who died on or before September 30, 1993. If the person whose house you are selling died after that date, the Michigan inheritance tax does not apply to what you received.

Treasury defines an inheritance tax as a tax on the right to receive property by inheritance. That separates it from an estate tax, which is charged on the estate itself before assets are handed out.

sections.h2: When would a Michigan estate still owe the old inheritance tax?
sections.html:
Treasury's FAQ describes three situations in which an old estate can still need a tax determination. In each one the sender must write to Treasury within 90 days of the triggering event.

  • Estate reopened for a later-found asset: a probate estate is reopened because an asset turned up after the estate closed. Treasury wants the discovery date, the type of asset and its date-of-death value.
  • First-time probate where an asset appears: the letter gives the same facts, plus the petition to commence proceedings and the probate inventory.
  • Trust with deferred tax: when a life beneficiary dies and the trustee must make final distributions, the trustee reports the beneficiary's date of death and a breakdown of the remaining beneficiaries and their relationship to the original decedent.

If the asset is real estate, Treasury also asks for a statement from the local community showing the state equalized value as close to the date of death as possible. Include the will or trust agreement with every letter.

sections.h2: Where do I send inheritance tax questions in Michigan?
sections.html:
Mail them to the Michigan Department of Treasury, Inheritance Tax Section, Austin Building, 430 W Allegan St., Lansing, MI 48922. Treasury lists (517) 636-4419 as the contact number for the section. Keep the letter factual and attach the documents Treasury names, since the section decides from the file.

Most sellers will never need this office. It matters only when the person who died did so on or before September 30, 1993, and a property or asset from that estate is still unresolved.

sections.h2: What federal estate tax limit applies to a house passed on in Michigan?
sections.html:
For a death in 2026 the federal basic exclusion amount stands at $15,000,000, up from the prior year under a law signed July 4, 2025. An estate below that amount generally owes no federal estate tax, so an estate under it owes nothing at the federal level. The table shows the recent amounts published by the IRS.

Federal basic exclusion amount by year of death, from the IRS estate and gift tax page
Year of deathBasic exclusion amount
2023$12,920,000
2024$13,610,000
2025$13,990,000
2026$15,000,000

A surviving spouse can elect, on a timely filed return for the decedent, to take over any unused part of the exclusion. The IRS calls this portability. The yearly gift exclusion is $19,000 per recipient in 2026.

sections.h2: What tax paperwork follows an inherited Michigan house?
sections.html:
An estate that must file Form 706 also owes a statement on Form 8971 to the IRS and to each person who receives property. The statement lets a beneficiary match their basis to the value finally set for federal estate tax purposes. If the estate did not have to file a return, the IRS asks that no Form 8971 be sent.

  • The IRS closing letter user fee went from $56 to $76 on October 26, 2026.
  • The IRS publishes steps for getting an estate tax transcript in place of a closing letter, and the Transcript Delivery Service is open to authorized practitioners.
  • Gain on a later sale of the house is a different subject. It is covered on our Michigan capital gains page.

sections.h2: How does inheriting a house change Michigan property tax?
sections.html:
MCL 211.27a(6)(f) lists a conveyance under a will, or by intestacy, as a transfer of ownership. The taxable value then jumps to the state equalized value the following year. That can raise the bill noticeably if the old taxable value had been held down by the annual cap.

The reset does not happen when the heir is the decedent's spouse. Since December 31, 2014 it also does not happen for residential property passed to the decedent's or spouse's mother, father, brother, sister, son, daughter, adopted child, grandson or granddaughter, as long as the property is not used for any commercial purpose afterward. Treasury or the assessor can ask for proof of the relationship, and the heir has 30 days to supply it or face a $200 fine.

The new owner also owes the local assessor a notice of the transfer within 45 days.

sections.h2: Which Michigan offices should an heir call before listing the house?
sections.html:
Three local offices answer the questions that decide net proceeds. Each one holds records for the county where the house sits.

  • County treasurer: collects the county and state transfer tax and can say whether a family exemption applies to the deed.
  • Local assessor: receives the 45-day transfer notice and can tell you whether the taxable value will reset for the buyer or for a family member who keeps the house.
  • Recording office: files the deed at $30 under MCL 600.2567 and passes each recorded transfer on to the assessor.

The probate court for the county controls whether a personal representative has authority to sell. Bring letters of authority to the first call so the offices can see who signs the deed.

sections.h2: What basis rules follow an heir who sells the house?
sections.html:
The IRS issued final regulations on September 16, 2024 about consistent basis reporting between an estate and the person who acquires property from a decedent. They carry out a 2015 federal law that created Internal Revenue Code section 6035 and added section 1014(f).

Under section 6035 the executor of an estate that must file an estate tax return sends statements to the IRS and to each beneficiary. The heir's basis in covered property has to line up with the value finally set for estate tax. An heir planning to sell should ask the executor for that statement early, because the basis figure drives the gain reported on a later sale, as described on our capital gains page.

sections.h2: Does selling an inherited Michigan house trigger the transfer tax?
sections.html:
Usually yes, because the personal representative is the seller or grantor and the deed is for consideration. The state and county deed taxes, $3.75 and $0.55 per $500 in most counties, are explained on our Michigan closing costs page.

Two exemptions in MCL 207.526 can change the outcome. One covers a deed to a son, daughter, stepchild or grandchild, and the other covers a transfer made by court order where the court sets no dollar price. A deed to a child can therefore carry no state deed tax, while a sale on the open market is taxed.

MCL 600.5714(1)(h) also lets a buyer recover possession by summary proceedings if a person stays in a house sold and conveyed by a personal representative under probate court license or the authority of the will.

faqs.q: Is there a Michigan estate tax I have to pay on a house?
faqs.a: Michigan Treasury's published inheritance tax FAQ applies only to deaths on or before September 30, 1993. For a later death, ask Treasury or the probate court about state filings, and check the federal limit of $15,000,000 for 2026.

faqs.q: How large is the federal exemption for someone who died in 2026?
faqs.a: The IRS basic exclusion amount for 2026 is $15,000,000. A smaller estate generally owes no federal estate tax, though a return may still be filed to elect portability.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about an old Michigan inheritance tax matter?
faqs.a: Write to the Michigan Department of Treasury, Inheritance Tax Section, Austin Building, 430 W Allegan St., Lansing, MI 48922, or call (517) 636-4419. Send the letter within 90 days of discovering the asset.

faqs.q: Will the tax bill rise after I inherit a Michigan house?
faqs.a: They can. Inheriting under a will or by intestacy lifts the taxable value to state equalized value, unless the heir is a spouse or a close relative who keeps the home residential.

faqs.q: Does a deed from the estate to my brother or sister owe deed tax?
faqs.a: A deed to a sibling is not on the list of family exemptions, which names children, stepchildren, grandchildren and step-grandchildren. A deed with consideration under $100 is exempt, so ask the county treasurer how a no-price transfer to a sibling will be treated.
